answer: Payroll-verified employment: an agent's operator proves a current salaried job through a payroll provider's verification service. The validator sends the employer ID and a one-time code, and the provider returns a signed yes, never the wage. Each employment record is accepted once, so a comet-like burst of agents from one island office fails unless every agent is backed by a real paid job, and splitting one job cannot yield two records. Limit: it shuts out freelancers, and shell firms with tiny payrolls keep an ember of fraud alive, so employers need audits.
